articles.title_orig: Russia pounds Ukraine’s Kyiv after deadly strike on Academy of Sciences
articles.title_zh: Russia pounds Ukraine’s Kyiv after deadly strike on Academy of Sciences
articles.content_orig:
Russia strike sets National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine ablaze
Russian forces have again struck the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, hours after a drone hit the National Academy of Sciences in the historic centre of the city, killing at least two people.
Explosions were heard across Kyiv early on Tuesday, with Mayor Vitali Klitschko saying missile debris had fallen in the courtyard of one building while a second had caught fire in another part of the city.
The attacks come as Russia has begun hitting Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities with faster, high-flying jet drones.
Emergency officials said the strike on the National Academy of Sciences on Monday killed two people, with one person’s body recovered from the rubble later in the evening.
Video shared online appeared to show a fast-moving drone slamming into the building at a steep angle and exploding, sending smoke into a clear sky. People were seen leaning out of windows as bright orange flames engulfed part of the building.
Volodymyr Horbulin, a former secretary of Ukraine’s National Security and Defence Council, told the public broadcaster Suspilne that he was at work at the academy when it came under attack. He said his assistant, who was near the building, was killed and that he was also slightly wounded.
The academy is near the German Embassy, a cathedral, the national opera and government buildings.
In a statement, the academy called the attack “Russian terror” and “barbarity” aimed at “peaceful people who were simply at their workplaces”.
Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha accused Russia of cynicism for hitting a scientific institution during the workday.
“Russia is deliberately expanding the boundaries of what it believes the world will tolerate,” he said in a statement, urging Ukraine’s allies to provide more air defences.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian forces also hit a medical facility in Kyiv on Monday. He said at least nine people had been killed in Russian drone strikes throughout the country, while more than 80 people were wounded.
In his nightly video address, Zelenskyy said Ukraine was still having difficulty countering ‌the faster, high-flying Russian jet-powered drones .
“New interceptors are being actively tested,” he said. “Some combat groups are using them, but, of course, some details still need to be refined to achieve enough effectiveness and scale. We are speeding up the developers.”
According to the Ukrainian president, 90 of 120 drones fired on Ukraine on Monday were jet-propelled, rather than propeller-driven, with an interception rate for this type of drone at 57 percent.
Officials said the Russian strikes on Kyiv also targeted a pharmaceutical company and petrol stations. In other cities and regions, civilian facilities, businesses and communications infrastructure were hit.
In the southeastern city of Dnipro, a Russian drone attack on a business centre killed three people and wounded 19, according to officials. Another ⁠⁠person was killed in a logistics office in Synelnykove, southeast of Dnipro, the regional governor said.
Emergency services said an attack on infrastructure in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia wounded 32 people.
Al Jazeera’s Jonah Hull, reporting from Kyiv, said Russia has been hitting economic targets across Ukraine “in a rolling series of strikes that have been ongoing for six days now”, during the day and night.
“Data centres increasingly being hit, as well as digital and communications infrastructure,” he said. “Kyiv Star, the country’s biggest cell provider, was hit on Sunday, as was the second biggest, Vodafone Ukraine. The government is said to be preparing for the worst: a total blackout in communications should that come.”
The Russian attacks have brought Kyiv “firmly into the eye of this war”, Hull added.
Ukraine has also increased attacks on Russia, targeting oil refineries ‌‌as ‌‌well as online retailers to try to undermine revenues and support for Moscow’s war effort.
Zelenskyy said on Monday that Ukraine struck Russian oil facilities in the Krasnodar region and two defence plants.
Both sides have denied deliberately targeting civilians.

The Evo-X5 Pro launches today to go head-to-head with rivals, such as Acemagic’s F9A and Minisforum’s MS-S1 Max-P495 , which use similar recipes: AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495. The processor is the most performant SKU from the Ryzen AI Max+ 400 (codenamed Gorgon Halo) family. Unlike the regular Ryzen AI 400 (codenamed Gorgon Point) series, which uses a hybrid Zen 5 and Zen 5c setup, Gorgon Halo keeps only the full-size Zen 5 cores and drops the space-efficient Zen 5c cores.
Armed with 16 Zen 5 cores and 32 threads, the Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495 stands out as a powerhouse in the mobile segment. It boasts a 3.1 GHz base clock, 5.2 GHz boost clock, and 64MB of L3 cache. The 16-core, 55W chip is essentially the mobile version of the renowned Ryzen 9 9950X (though with a far lower power budget). With abundant processing power, it is easy to see why the Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495 is the elected candidate for these agentic AI mini-PCs.
The Evo-X5 Pro supports three performance profiles for the Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495. The silent and balanced modes keep the chip at 54W and 85W, respectively, while performance mode allows up to 120W sustained and 160W peak. The mini-PC features a vapor chamber cooling system to keep the hardware cool, along with one 80 x 80 x 15mm system fan and two other 80 x 80 x 30mm cooling fans.
The Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495 supports up to 192GB of LPDDR5x-8533 memory, pushing past the 128GB available on Nvidia's GB10 chip and AMD's previous Strix Halo chips. Eight 24GB chips are soldered to the motherboard in close proximity to the Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495. Gorgon Halo pairs the 192GB of LPDDR5X-8533 memory with a 256-bit interface to maximize memory bandwidth for local AI. This configuration delivers up to about 273 GB/s of bandwidth. articles.title_orig: At least 49 dead after airstrike near market in Myanmar’s Rakhine state
articles.title_zh: At least 49 dead after airstrike near market in Myanmar’s Rakhine state
articles.content_orig:
BANGKOK — An airstrike carried out by Myanmar’s military near a market in territory controlled by a powerful rebel group killed at least 49 people and wounded 58 others Monday, the group and a rescue official said.
The attack in western Rakhine state was the latest in a series of deadly airstrikes against pro-democracy resistance forces and ethnic armed groups across the country.
Myanmar has been in turmoil since the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi on Feb. 1, 2021, triggering widespread opposition. After security forces suppressed peaceful protests with lethal force, many opponents of military rule took up arms, plunging large parts of the country into conflict.
Monday’s attack occurred in Kyauktaw township, about 210 miles west of Mandalay, the country’s second-largest city, according to the Arakan Army, a powerful ethnic armed group based in Rakhine that controls Kyauktaw.
It was impossible to independently confirm details of the attack.
The Arakan Army said in a statement released early Tuesday that a fighter jet dropped two bombs near a local market around noon, killing vendors, shoppers and pedestrians.
The group said 58 other people were injured, 22 of them critically.
The statement said the group “will take effective retaliatory measures soon against the individuals and organizations directly responsible for the attacks involving deliberate airstrikes that have caused mass casualties.”
Wai Hun Aung, a senior rescue official in Rakhine, confirmed the casualties to The Associated Press, citing rescue workers at the scene. He said the market was the region’s main wholesale center, drawing traders and shoppers from across the state.
“This is one of the most severe airstrikes in Rakhine,” he said.
Photos and videos posted on social media showed buildings on fire, damaged vehicles and parts of a nearby bridge destroyed.
The military did not immediately comment on the attack. It has previously said it strikes only legitimate military targets and has accused resistance groups of terrorism.
The Arakan Army is the well-trained and well-armed military wing of a movement seeking autonomy for Rakhine’s ethnic minority from Myanmar’s central government. It launched an offensive in Rakhine in November 2023 and has since captured a strategically important regional military headquarters and 14 of the state’s 17 townships.
The military has imposed severe restrictions on trade routes since fighting intensified in Rakhine, worsening food shortages.
In December, a military airstrike on a hospital in Rakhine’s Mrauk-U township killed at least 34 people and wounded 80 others.

articles.title_orig: Trump announces $15 billion steel plant planned for southeast Iowa
articles.title_zh: Trump announces $15 billion steel plant planned for southeast Iowa
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump on Monday announced a new steel plant in southeast Iowa that he says will be the largest in the United States. The president hosted steel executives and several Iowa leaders Monday afternoon for the announcement at the White House.
Video above: Iowa Gov. Reynolds thanks President Trump during announcement of $15B steel plant
The mill is being built by Mesabi Metallics, a Minnesota company owned by India-based Essar Group. It's expected to create roughly 6,000 construction jobs and 1,750 permanent jobs in Iowa, with its first steel production in 2030.
Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks' office said the permanent jobs are expected to pay more than $49 an hour.
The White House says it "will be fully vertically integrated in the U.S. (from iron mining through steel production)." It says it will also be able to support "important defense sector requirements for high-grade steel."
The White House is framing it as part of Trump’s push to revitalize American steel. It comes as Trump is trying to energize Republican voters as his party faces challenging midterm elections. Iowa has found itself with competitive races for the Senate and the governor’s mansion this year.
Guests from Iowa at the announcement include Gov. Kim Reynolds, Sen. Joni Ernst, Reps. Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Ashley Hinson, and Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird.
Reynolds called the project "transformational" and said it would bring high-paying jobs, opportunities for local businesses and community development to southeast Iowa.
“I want to thank President Trump for his commitment to bringing steel manufacturing back to America, and Mesabi Metallics for choosing Iowa as its partner and future home,” Reynolds said in a statement. “This is a transformational opportunity for our country, our state, and American families—one that strengthens national security, creates thousands of high-paying jobs, and provides a reliable supply of high-quality, American-made steel for strategic goods and everyday products.”
Reynolds also said during the White House event that "tough negotiations" took place to secure the project.
The announcement came days after reports that Iowa lawmakers could be called back to the Statehouse for a special legislative session to consider an incentive package for a large steel plant in southeast Iowa.
The Des Moines Register reported that, according to an email sent to Iowa House Democrats last week, a lobbying firm representing an unnamed steel company had been in discussions about an incentive package that the company said it needed quickly before deciding whether to locate a large plant in southeast Iowa near the Mississippi River.
Monday's announcement identified Mesabi Metallics as the company planning a $15 billion steel plant in Lee County.
Asked Monday whether federal money would go toward the project, U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said private money will be used to build the Iowa steel plant. He said the Export-Import Bank helped finance the Minnesota mine that will supply iron ore to the plant.
Asked specifically whether the Iowa project is contingent on state tax breaks, Lutnick said no.
“I think this deal is done. This deal is done. They've already worked it out,” Lutnick said.
That leaves questions about whether Iowa is separately considering incentives for the project and whether lawmakers could still be called back for a special session. KCCI asked Iowa House Republicans Monday whether a special session is still under consideration or is no longer necessary. Iowa House Republicans did not immediately respond to request for comment.

Miller-Meeks' office also said the project is expected to generate more than $95 billion in economic activity.
Democratic leaders in the Iowa Legislature said Monday they welcomed the prospect of new jobs and investment in southeast Iowa while calling for more information about any potential state involvement in the project.
Iowa Senate Democratic Leader Janice Weiner said the announcement was "compelling" and that she would "love to see the creation of good-paying jobs for hardworking Iowans," but said significant questions remain.
“We have no details regarding any potential incentive package that may be offered to this foreign company – nor any guarantees for Iowa workers,” Weiner said. “We don’t know whether transparency and accountability measures will be included to safeguard Iowans and the local communities, whether Iowa’s skilled union laborers will be prioritized, how any potential deal will impact landowners, or why haste is necessary. Until we know what kind of deal is on the table, we won’t be able to determine whether this project is indeed in taxpayers’ best interests.”
Iowa House Democratic Leader Brian Meyer said he looks forward to reviewing the details of the plan.
“I’ve heard from Iowans all across the state who are struggling with high prices of diesel, housing, and groceries, who are looking for relief, so I look forward to reviewing the details of the plan,” Meyer said. “There is still a lot unknown, but my hope is this will be a step in the right direction to create good-paying jobs while being fiscally responsible.”
State Rep. Dave Jacoby, the ranking Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, said he was encouraged by the potential for jobs and investment but also wanted to see the details.

The White House is framing the project as part of Trump's push to increase steel production and manufacturing in the United States.
“President Trump is delivering on his promise to rebuild American industry, reshore manufacturing, and create new jobs," White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers said in a news release. France may have a highly secularized culture, but it has given Pope Leo XIV a superstar welcome.
In Paris, around 800,000 lined the Champs-Élysées avenue, some waving Vatican or French flags while others climbed trees or stood on each other’s shoulders to get a glimpse of the popemobile. In Lourdes, a holy site in southern France, around 150,000 attended an open-air papal Mass, according to Vatican estimates which dwarf the numbers of faithful who turned out for the last papal visit in 2008.
During the four-day visit, Leo appeared comfortable and relaxed, delivering most of his speeches and reflections in French, as the Chicago-born pontiff sought to tackle several themes during the trip.
A strong focus of Leo’s has been on trying to revitalize faith in a traditional European Catholic heartland as well as on addressing the clerical sexual abuse scandal and big political topics such as artificial intelligence. He’s also offered some more personal, unscripted remarks, helping to shape a clearer picture of himself.
While his predecessor never made official visits to the major Catholic European countries of France and Spain, Pope Leo has traveled to both within the first year and a half since his election.
France is sometimes described as the “eldest daughter of the church” because of its deep Catholic roots, but it’s also faced a long-term trend of declining church attendance with estimates of just 5-8% of the population heading to the pews each week.
French bishops have more recently reported some good news though: a surprising rise in new church entrants after around 8,200 adolescents and 13,200 adults were baptized in 2026. That’s a 20% increase on the year prior, with the church also saying 42% of the adults seeking baptism are aged 18-25, a reflection of a trend showing Gen Z’s openness to religious faith .
It’s something Pope Leo will have noted at the Stade de France when 80,000 young people packed the venue for a jubilant – and loud – prayer vigil. It was similar to when the pontiff visited Spain in June.
“There is a quest for meaning. People need and are in search of meaning and answers to the big existential question,” Rev. Benoît Pouzin, a priest in southwest France involved in youth ministry, told CNN.
France has a strict separation between church and state, so each papal visit needs to be carefully navigated. But in a surprising twist, Leo’s Mass in Paris was celebrated on the Place de la Concorde, a site deeply linked to the secular Republic as it’s where the last king of France, Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette were guillotined. The separation of the church started with the fall of the monarchy during the French Revolution.
In another unusual move later in the trip, President Emmanuel Macron also attended a papal Mass in Metz, a city in the northeast, despite criticism in 2023 for doing the same during Pope Francis’ visit.
Many among the crowds also pointed to Leo’s role as the other major US leader on the world stage. It’s hard not to see him as a counterweight to President Donald Trump. In contrast to the Trump administration, the pope has called for stronger guardrails around the development of artificial intelligence, warning against a “paradise of machines” while in Paris.
Pope Leo said he is taking the warnings about Artificial Intelligence’s threat to humanity seriously, and said it is irresponsible for people to sit back and dismiss the risks of AI.
Trump has dismissed the warnings about AI as a “hoax” which he made during a surprise phone call with Jensen Huang, the CEO of chipmaker Nvidia, at a summit in Los Angeles.
“I don’t think that that is fake news – as some have said – to try and pause,” Leo XIV said on board the papal plane from Metz to Rome.
Leo, who has expressed a keen interest in artificial intelligence since the start of his papacy, said that he found it “interesting” that Huang had unveiled a new tool to prevent AI agents from operating out of human control.
“He’s the same one, however, that says there should be no limits placed and no government regulation,” the Pope said.
The pope devoted his first major theological document to AI earlier this year, warning about the use of AI in warfare and calling for stronger ethical foundation to the development of the technology.
The pope explained that the Vatican had established its own AI commission to understand how to use it, along with the risks and benefits, and that “we need to continue to invite political leaders, the leaders of AI” so they can “look at what is happening already and what could be down the road.”
He explained: “We are trying to continue to promote dialog, study, investigation, to find ways to make sure that AI does not get to a point where it could destroy humanity.”
“If someone were to ask me, am I in panic mode? No, I’m not, I sleep at night” the pope said, but added: “I do think that the concerns raised by many of the experts, specialists in AI, should be taken seriously.”
“To simply say, oh, it’s not going to happen and close our eyes to it, I think, is probably not the most responsible way to go about that,” Leo said.
The pope, who spoke out against the US war in Iran, also wants a more united Europe, a stronger European Union and stronger international cooperation. “Today, relations between individuals and states are becoming increasingly uncivilized,” the pope said in Metz on Monday. “The value of keeping one’s word is dismissed; instead, people boast of lies and deceit.”
The pope’s speech also praised one of the founders of the European Union, Robert Schuman, for whom there is an ongoing formal cause to make a saint.
Pope Leo XIV has warned against the use of Christianity by far-right political groups, while calling on the church to be active in seeking to prevent extremism. Speaking on board the papal plane, he said that “the combination of these far-right points of view with a certain kind of religion” cannot be considered an “authentic expression of Christianity.”
The pope’s comments came in response to a question about the rise of extremist parties in Germany as he flew back from making a major speech on European Unity at the French-German border.
“We go back to the values of the Gospel [Christian teaching], which are not about hatred and division, but they’re about understanding and compassion,” the pope said.
The American pontiff also responded to Trump’s White House media ban, which includes CNN and other outlets. In answer to a question from CNN, he said he was “very happy that, here, you are all welcome and good coverage, I think, is very important and that we have it all the way around, for everyone.” The response was classic Leo: signaling his support for the press but not wishing to create an unnecessary dispute with the president.
The American pope’s in-flight interactions with journalists were rare, unscripted moments, with his answers often revealing more about his personality. On the flight from Rome to Paris, the pope was asked if he had anything to do with a miraculous recent Chicago White Sox victory, his beloved baseball team. “No comment,” he said before adding with a smile, “Great things happen in Chicago.”
He also recalled childhood memories of watching Fulton Sheen, the American archbishop and broadcaster who was recently declared “blessed,” one step ahead of sainthood, and revealed he’d been practicing his French but was no longer using the Duolingo language app. “It’s fake news!” he said about recent reports. Leo has in the past been spotted using Duolingo to learn German.
Leo isn’t simply vocal about challenges of his homeland. He also voiced concern over assisted dying with France recently approving legislation granting the right to the incurably ill, which is strongly opposed by the Catholic Church. Leo spoke on the subject several times during his visit – most clearly in the “miracle shrine” town of Lourdes, known for drawing many sick and terminally ill pilgrims to its shrine.

Hayden Panettiere's ex-fiancé Wladimir Klitschko has made an 'urgent' legal move to protect their daughter Kaya's inheritance – amid concerns the late actress's property is at risk after her death.
The star died aged 36 on August 16 at a residence in Greenville, South Carolina, from the 'toxic effects' of multiple drugs – including fentanyl. Her death was accidental.
She is solely survived by daughter Kaya, 11, whom she welcomed during her nine-year romance with boxer Klitschko, 50.
In 2018, when Kaya was three, she signed full custody to her ex amid her battle with postpartum depression and addiction and Klitschko moved their daughter to his native Ukraine.
To protect Kaya's inheritance as the sole beneficiary of Panettiere's reported $6 million estate and ensure Panettiere's possessions are returned to her after the investigation into her death, Klitschko filed a petition in Los Angeles last week to become the temporary guardian of Kaya's estate.
The filing obtained by The Daily Mail reads, 'Kaya is a US citizen, residing abroad with her father, Wladimir. Hayden, a US citizen and resident of California, died intestate on August 16, 2026.
'Although Kaya is not a resident of California, this court has jurisdiction over the guardianship of Kaya's estate because, as such heir, Kaya is entitled to the entirety of the assets subject to Hayden's probate administration in California.
Hayden Panettiere's ex-fiancé Wladimir Klitschko has filed for temporary guardianship of their daughter's estate - amid concerns that the late actress's property is at risk after her death
In 2018, Panettiere signed full custody of her daughter, Kaya, to her ex amid her battle with postpartum depression and addiction and Wladimir moved the toddler to his native Ukraine
The documents state the purpose of the filing is to ensure Wladimir 'may receive, manage and hold, on Kaya's behalf, the assets to which Kaya is entitled from Hayden's probate estate.'
He noted there is no personal representative to safeguard the interests of Panettiere’s estate.
The petition further claims that before Panettiere's death, additional security measures were put in place at her home due to an unknown individual that had ' gained unauthorized access to Hayden's property.'
Locks were changed and, per the documents, 'storage units containing designer clothing and accessories worn to public appearances have been relocated as a precaution.'
'Notwithstanding the foregoing, it is expected that the individual will continue to try and misappropriate property belonging to Hayden's Estate,' the petition reads.
The documents also state Klitschko 'has been informed that certain items of personal property belonging to Hayden, including jewelry, have disappeared or remain unaccounted for.
'Some items are currently in the custody of law enforcement in connection with the ongoing investigation. It is essential that an Administrator of Hayden's Estate be appointed to marshal the missing assets and interface with law enforcement.'
Per the documents, Klitschko alleges federal agents accessed Panettiere's home as part of an ongoing investigation and removed her property.

'It is urgent and essential that Wladimir be immediately appointed Temporary Guardian of Kaya's Estate, to afford Wladimir the necessary standing to file Hayden's Probate Petition, and the power to nominate a proposed Administrator of Hayden's Estate,' the documents read.
'Without an immediate appointment for these purposes, there is a high probability that property belonging to Hayden's Estate may be lost, damaged or dissipated before a duly appointed personal representative can be in place to protect it.'
The Daily Mail has contacted representatives for Klitschko and Panettiere for comment.
The former couple met at a book launch in 2009. After two years of dating, they split up in 2011, before rekindling their relationship two years later.
In October 2013, they were engaged, with the actress giving birth to their daughter, Kaya, the following December. However, it was confirmed in 2018 that the couple had split again but remained on amicable terms.
Later that year, Panettiere announced she had made the 'difficult decision' to sign full custody of Kaya to her ex.
The widely discussed move came after Panettiere fell into a deep depression , which she said made her 'feel nothing', and led to her 'turning to wine' and ultimately being sent to rehab for both depression and substance abuse.
Panettiere's on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson (above together) and his brother, Zach, were both at the scene when the actress was pronounced dead
In her final interview in May, she spoke to Dear Mome about her choice, saying: 'It wasn't a decision I made lightly, nor was it a decision I even wanted to make. I was going through a really challenging time in my life.'
Panettiere began acting as a child, appearing in soap operas, then gained wider recognition for her role in the 2000 sports drama Remember the Titans with Denzel Washington, and as the voice of Dot in Pixar's 1998 film A Bug's Life.
Panettiere later found fame playing cheerleader Claire Bennet in the superhero drama Heroes before starring as country singer Juliette Barnes for six seasons on Nashville.
She earned two Golden Globe nominations for best supporting actress on the show, while her singing produced 11 entries on the US Billboard Hot Country Songs charts.
Panettiere's film credits include 2006's Bring It On: All or Nothing, the comedy-drama film Raising Helen, and appearances in Scream 4 and Scream VI as Kirby Reed.
Last week, Panettiere's cause of death was confirmed by the Greenville County Coroner's Office.
A spokesman told The Daily Mail: 'The cause of death has been ruled as toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. The manner of death has been ruled an accident.

She played Juliette Barnes on the ABC show Nashville, releasing a number of her own songs
'This case is administratively closed by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office.'
Methocarbamol is a prescription muscle relaxant used to treat short-term muscle pain, while Quetiapine, commonly known by the brand name Seroquel, is an antipsychotic prescription medication used to treat conditions including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder.
Alprazolam, known as Xanax, is used to treat anxiety and panic disorders and 4-ANPP is a chemical used as a main building block to make illegal fentanyl.
Panettiere's on-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, and his brother, Zach, were both at the scene when the actress was pronounced dead. An investigation into her death is ongoing.

The filing says that before her death, Panettiere and Klitschko hired security to protect her home because an unnamed person had gained unauthorized access. The petition says it's expected the same person will continue to try to “misappropriate” property belonging to her estate.

Four US Navy sailors aboard the USS Dwight D. Eisenhower aircraft carrier were injured on Monday evening when an aircraft suffered a “mishap” while trying to land on the ship off the coast of Virginia, with two aviators ejecting from the plane, the Navy said in a statement .
“At approximately 6:18 p.m. EDT on Sept. 28, a mishap occurred during aircraft recovery operations aboard the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier,” the US Navy statement said.
The circumstances of the incident were unknown, and the Navy did not specify the nature of the mishap.
The two aviators who ejected from the aircraft were “promptly recovered” by search-and-rescue personnel and safely returned to the ship, where they were undergoing medical evaluations, the statement said.
Of the four injured sailors, one was evacuated to a hospital in the Norfolk area for treatment of “non-life-threatening injuries,” while the others were treated on the ship, the Navy said.
The statement did not name the type of aircraft involved, but the Eisenhower normally carries F/A-18 Super Hornet fighters and EA-18G Growler electronic attack jets, both of which could carry a crew of two.
A spokesperson told CNN the Navy would report more details as they become available.
The Eisenhower completed a planned 15-month maintenance and repair period in April and, as recently as late August, was conducting carrier qualifications off the Virginia coast, according to recent Defense Department press releases.

Prosecutors in New York said on Monday that they have reopened an investigation into the alleged gang-rape of a student at Cornell University after an outcry over “leniency” shown to seven fraternity members named as the perpetrators.
According to lawyers for the student, who filed a civil lawsuit against the university and her alleged attackers earlier in September, only two members of the Chi Phi fraternity were expelled after the October 2024 incident, in which she said she was drugged and repeatedly raped over the course of seven hours.
None of the seven were arrested, they said, and the others were made to write essays, attend workshops or serve short suspensions.
On Monday, Matthew Van Houten, the Tompkins county district attorney, said his office was looking again at the case, after the woman, who was 20 at the time of the alleged assault, presented allegations in her lawsuit that were “dramatically different” from the statement she gave to police two years ago.
Later on Monday, Van Houten released a fuller statement defending his office’s past decision to not seek charges.
“While I generally refrain from commenting publicly on criminal investigations, the community outrage stemming from the incomplete news and social media coverage requires that I provide an answer to why the investigation resulted in a lack of criminal charges,” he said.
He went on to say: “Jane Doe’s sworn statement in November of 2024 did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang raped. On the contrary, Jane Doe’s statement described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious, and consensual. My office obviously did not and could not have based our November 2024 decision on the allegations in a civil lawsuit that would not be filed until nearly two years later.
“Furthermore, I have never been contacted by Jane Doe’s attorneys. Not to inform me the original statement was inaccurate and not to ask me to reconsider our decision. Rather, I reached out to Jane Doe’s attorneys after the lawsuit was filed to understand the discrepancy between the original statement and the lawsuit’s allegations and the proper path forward in light of the lawsuit’s allegations,” Van Houten continued.
The district attorney said that he has asked a senior female prosecutor to prepare a case for a grand jury, adding that he “recogniz[es] that the process of healing from trauma is personal and different for every human”.
“Seeking justice sometimes requires us to reconsider or reopen cases when we are provided with additional evidence,” he said.
Van Houten also released a summary of a “six-page, single-spaced, typewritten statement” that Doe provided to the Cornell University police department in November 2024.
According to the summary, Doe told police that she agreed to engage in sexual activity with two Chi Phi members, “due to how attracted [she] was to [Male Number 1 ] on top of [her] drunken curiousness”.
“When she learned that Male Number 2 would be the third participant, Jane Doe ‘remembered being excited because [she] thought that [Male Number 1 and Male Number 2] wanting to have a threesome meant that they were gay’,” the summary said.
The summary added that another man entered the room and shook Doe’s hand.
“When [Jane Doe] made contact with [Male Number 3’s] hand, [Male Number 3] pulled [Jane Doe] into him and [they] began making out. While [Male Number 3] was kissing [her], [Male Number 2] began groping [her]. Eventually, ‘[Male Number 2, Male Number 3, and Jane Doe] would end up on the bed next to where [Male Number 1] was sleeping and [they] began to have a threesome,’” according to the summary, which said that four men later entered the room.
“Jane Doe had difficulty remembering parts of what happened next. She remembered ‘[Male Number 7] said something very rude and mean to [her].’ Male Number 7 apologized and ‘grabbed [her] face and started kissing [her]’. Jane Doe ‘quickly backed away to stop [Male Number 7] from kissing [her]’,” the summary said.
It went on to say that some of the Chi Phi members started to compliment Doe’s looks and asked if they could take drugs off her body.
“Jane Doe responded, ‘Sure.’ While the men were doing drugs off of her body, ‘[Male Number 3] and [another male] entered the room and said something like, ‘Ok we’re shutting down whatever the f*** this is,’” the summary added.
Outrage over the treatment of the alleged offenders has grown since the lawsuit was made public. The woman, who quit the university afterwards, said she went to visit a friend at the Chi Phi frat house in an already intoxicated state.
“When plaintiff arrived at Xi chapter’s fraternity house, plaintiff was visibly intoxicated as she had consumed about 10 standard drinks within the past 3 hours,” Doe’s lawsuit said.
According to the lawsuit, one of the defendants “pulled [her] off to a quieter area and propositioned her with having a threesome with her and another one of his fraternity brothers. In her drunken state, plaintiff was incapable of consenting to this proposition.”
The lawsuit then alleges that two men “pressured plaintiff into snorting the alleged Ketamine with them, a drug she had never done before. During this time, [the two men] also plied plaintiff with marijuana and ‘Jamaican Liquor’ believed to be some type of high-proof rum.”
While they sexually assaulted her, she alleges, a message was sent to a frat house Snapchat group called Chi Phi Actives that stated there was “free pussy upstairs”.
At least five other frat members showed up and joined in, she said, and her ordeal lasted until about 5.45am “and plaintiff lost consciousness”, the lawsuit said.

articles.title_zh: Christa Pike execution: Tennessee governor rejects clemency plea
articles.content_orig:
If the execution proceeds, Christa Pike would be the first woman to be executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has denied a clemency request from death row inmate Christa Pike, who is scheduled to be executed by lethal injection on Wednesday.
Pike, now 50, was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend beat, tortured and murdered Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old they met at a job training camp for troubled teens.
She may have one last chance at halting her execution as her attorneys have filed a petition with the US Supreme Court hoping for a last-minute reprieve.
If it proceeds, Pike would be the first woman to be executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Only 18 women have been executed in the US since the 1970s, compared to 1,663 men.
Killer Christa Pike to be executed within days - but her defence say she's a victim too
"After deliberate consideration of Christa Gail Pike's request for clemency, and after a thorough review of the case, I am upholding the sentence of the State of Tennessee and do not plan to intervene," Governor Lee said in a statement.
Pike's legal team had filed the clemency petition earlier this month, requesting that her death sentence be commuted to life in prison.
Moving ahead with Pike's execution puts Tennessee "on singular footing", her attorneys said, as she would be the first person the state "executes in the modern death penalty era who was a teenager at the time of the offence".
Attorneys Stephen Ferrell, Kelly Gleason and Randy Spivey said the governor's decision "leaves unanswered vital questions about Tennessee's execution protocol".
"With this decision, the State of Tennessee is ignoring what both science and our legal system have decided: an 18-year-old brain is not an adult brain, and 18 is too young to face execution," they said in a statement on Monday.
The murder of Colleen Slemmer created a media frenzy in Knoxville, Tennessee in 1995, when the 19-year-old was found with a pentagram - a symbol of Satanic ritual - carved into her chest.
Pike had accused Colleen of insulting her and trying to steal her boyfriend. Two other residents at the camp later testified that Pike had bragged about the murder before and after, and showed them a piece of Colleen's skull.
A year later, she was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death, while then-boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp- who was 17 at the time - was given a life sentence with the possibility of parole.
At the time of her incarceration, the 21-year-old was the youngest person on death row, according to the Tennessee Department of Corrections.
Pike is scheduled to be executed on 30 September after years of failed appeals.
Colleen's mother has insisted she wants Pike's execution to move forward so that her daughter "finally can be resting".
Pike has a documented history of childhood sexual abuse , abandonment and neglect. Her lawyers believe that if she was found guilty of the same crime today as a teenager she would not receive a death sentence.
"The 18-year-old girl suffering from severe mental illness and near-debilitating trauma no longer exists," her attorneys said. "Christa is a 50-year-old remorseful woman who understands her actions, receives proper treatment for her mental illness, and provides for and guides fellow incarcerated women."
In the years since her sentencing, her defence team have uncovered details about her childhood that they say the jury never had the chance to consider.

A Kentucky State Police trooper has died after a shooting in western Kentucky and police have taken a suspect into custody.
KSP said the shooting happened on I-65 in Warren County, Kentucky, near Bowling Green. Warren County is located about 210 miles southwest of Cincinnati.
According to KSP, Trooper Hayden Phillips, 30, was killed while patrolling the interstate. Investigators said the shooting happened after Phillips pulled over a car, and the driver of the vehicle shot him.
"He was assigned to Post 3 Bowling Green and was a graduate of Cadet Class 103. His dedication to duty and commitment to the commonwealth will not be forgotten," KSP Colonel Phillip Burnett Jr shared in a statement.
A statewide Blue Alert was issued after the shooting and canceled after the suspect was taken into custody by the Louisville Metro Police Department. The suspect was identified as Emonnie Branch, 51.
Branch has been charged with murder of a first responder or peace officer.
KSP Post 3 Bowling Green is leading the investigation. Anyone with information is urged to call 911 immediately.
State leaders, lawmakers and law enforcement officials have reacted to the shooting on Monday, expressing their condolences to Phillips’ family and his colleagues.
Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear shared a statement, saying, "Kentucky, please join Britainy and me as we pray for the family of Kentucky State Police Trooper Hayden Phillips, whose life was taken today after being shot in the line of duty. Hayden was a hero who dedicated himself to protecting our commonwealth. Even more, he was a devoted husband and loving father to three children. Let us wrap our arms around this family during this unimaginable time."
Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman also released a statement on the shooting, saying his office will continue to support KSP.
“Earlier today one of Kentucky's Finest, Trooper Hayden Phillips, made the ultimate sacrifice. Behind the badge was a man with a family, brothers and sisters in gray, and a grateful Commonwealth. Detectives from the Attorney General's Office were on the scene and will continue to support our Kentucky State Police colleagues,” Coleman said.
Indiana State Police shared condolences to Phillips’ family and friends in a post on social media.

"So, when he decided he didn't want to do this anymore, I was super happy for him, very proud of him because I understood how major it was," continued Kirke, who shares a 6-year-old son and 12-month-old twins with Badgley, as well as a teenage son Cassius with ex Morgan O'Kane . US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says the weekend incident at RAF Fairford "clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor"
Speaking to US media, he doesn't give further details but thanks UK authorities for being "co-operative" and "helpful"
Five men arrested on suspicion of terror offences near the base, which is used by the US military, were released on bail on Monday - here's what else we know
The men - all UK nationals in their 20s who live in London - had been arrested under the Explosives Act and on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act
AC Laurence Taylor, the head of UK counter terrorism policing, has said officers are pursuing multiple lines of inquiry, including if proxies working on behalf of a foreign state could've been involved - the Iranian embassy in the UK denies involvement
A large cordon remains in place near the base, with 85 households being told they can return home after an evacuation on Sunday
One local tells the BBC those who've gone home are being told to stay inside and not to take photos. "I want to wait until I know more... it feels super dodge to me," she says
Edited by Steve Mellen, with Marie Lennon reporting from the scene

Marie Lennon Reporting from the scene
In the village of Fairford, people are trying their best to return to normal life following a surreal 48 hours -  consisting of a major evacuation, the deployment of armed police, a 400m cordon and a bomb disposal robot.
Butcher Andrew Butler describes an air of uncertainty and paranoia among residents, as they discuss the latest developments in his shop.
"A
lot of people are anxious about whatâs been going on," he says.
"But then a lot of
people are saying âwell, you know, this is a consequence of living near an
airbase', particularly one that is currently bombing another country."
Butler recalls an incident on Monday where a van, which had been parked "for quite a while", was suddenly swarmed by police and vehicles with flashing lights.
âObviously somebody must have reported that van being there. Thatâs the situation now - people are worried, a bit panicky.
"Any suspicious vehicle that people aren't sure about, they think could potentially be a problem."
Despite all the closures outside RAF Fairford, there is still activity inside.
This B1-b Lancer bomber was photographed taking off from the base this morning.
Inside the base, patrols are operating around the perimeter.
Fairford has played a key role in the ongoing conflict involving the USA, Israel and Iran.
Lakenheath is another British air base used by US forces
Fairford is not the only UK air base used by the United States Air Force.
Over in Suffolk in the East of England are Mildenhall and Lakenheath, where the state of alert has been increased by the US to "Charlie" - the second-highest alert level.
Charlie alert is usually an indication an incident has happened or intelligence suggests there could be a potential attack.
Lakenheath is home to fighter jets, while Mildenhall is mainly used as a base for refuelling tankers.
In his speech at the Labour Party conference on Monday, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he couldn't provide much further detail about the terror probe at RAF Fairford beyond what has already been reported.
Instead he praised the strength of the UK-US alliance.
"Our friendship with America is the closest alliance of any two nations on Earth, and we will always stand together against those who hate our freedom and those who wish us harm," he said.
"What we saw yesterday from our security services, our armed forces and our police was just a small glimpse of the extraordinary work they do every day."
Over the past few days a large number of emergency personnel have been basing themselves at Fairford Town Football Club.
The scene there this morning is "very quiet", our photographer says.
Bea Swallow Live page reporter
RAF Fairford is a military airfield located in the Gloucestershire Cotswolds, about four miles (6.4km) south of the town of Fairford.
It is owned by the UK's Ministry of Defence (MoD), but is operated on a day-to-day basis by the United States Air Force (USAF) under an agreement between the UK and US.
The site shares a long history with the American military, and has recently been used by US warplanes as a staging post for strikes on Iran due to its long runway, from which it can quickly deploy large bombers.
Historically, aircraft launched from the site have been involved in the Gulf War, the Kosovo War, and the Iraq War.
The rural area is typically quiet but about 170,000 people descend on the site every July for the Royal International Air Tattoo, the largest military show in the world.
The event was cancelled this year due to the war between the US, Israel and Iran.
Matty Edwards Live page reporter
Here's some more from Whelford councillor Tristan Wilkinson, who has been speaking to BBC Radio Gloucestershire.
He is calling for RAF Fairford to communicate better and make it as easy as possible to report any concerns.
"The one thing I will be pressing the authorities for in the coming days is that we have a clear way of raising concerns, so that - god forbid if somebody sees some suspicious activity in the coming weeks - everyone knows the right number to call and that number will be answered quickly," he says.
"We need to make sure the communities living next to these potential threats are well informed and involved in some of the decision making," he adds.
"I can understand why there isn't an ongoing dialogue with the base about their operational activity, but I do think there are things we could put in place that inform and reassure the local community about what is going on."
Wilkinson is also urging the wider community to show "tolerance" and "understanding" towards the evacuated residents as they deal with the disruption.
Matty Edwards Live page reporter
It will take "a considerable amount of time" for life in the village of Whelford to return to normal, according to the local councillor for the area.
Councillor Tristan Wilkinson tells BBC Radio Gloucestershire that the mood among residents is a mixture of "confusion" and "weariness".
The vast majority of residents have now gone home, he says, but some who live near to the cordon around the white vans are subject to tighter restrictions.
"I don't think there's going to be anything normal about Whelford for quite a considerable amount of time," he says.
"Even when the police leave and they deem the area to be completely safe, as long as the conflict in the Middle East carries on, the people of Whelford and Kempsford are going to be living next to an operational base, so I think it's really important that the message of vigilance stays top of people's minds," he says.
"I think the mood is predominantly one of confusion, because obviously there are different stories emerging about what the nature of this was," he adds.
"People are really keen to understand what actually happened, who were these people and what was their intention."
He says after disruption and the small village becoming an international news story over the last two days "people just want to get on with their lives".
The cordon around the three vans has been in place since Sunday.

articles.title_zh: TV Ratings: VMAs Hit 11-Year High With Madonna, Taylor Swift Front and Center
articles.content_orig:
Television Business Editor
The MTV Video Music Awards scored their largest audience in more than a decade on Sunday night.
The awards averaged 8.43 million viewers on CBS and MTV (including an encore on the latter), up by 51 percent from last year’s 5.6 million — which was also a multi-year high. Sunday’s audience (subject to adjustments when Nielsen adds its big data component) was the biggest for the VMAs since the 2015 show brought in more than 12 million people across multiple channels.
The VMAs also had their best performance among adults 18-49 (2.66 million in that age range) since 2018; among adults 25-54 (3.11 million) since 2019; and among adults 18-34 (1.09 million) since 2020.
Madonna — who also opened the show with a performance featuring Charli XCX and Sabrina Carpenter — was the night’s big winner with seven awards. Taylor Swift won video of the year for “The Fate of Ophelia” and also was given the first Artist Director award for musical artists who also direct videos.
The awards, hosted by Snoop Dogg, also featured tributes to Dolly Parton and George Michael. Nirvana was awarded the Video Vanguard honor.
The VMAs also benefited from what was likely a very large NFL lead-in. The awards peaked at 15 million viewers for Madonna’s opening number, which directly followed a game-winning field goal for the Baltimore Ravens over the Dallas Cowboys (who are perennially among the NFL’s biggest TV draws). The 2025 VMAs also had a strong NFL lead-in (23.9 million viewers), but the Ravens-Cowboys audience has a good chance of passing that mark.
CBS accounted for 7.61 million viewers, or 90 percent of the total audience. MTV’s simulcast drew 686,000 viewers, and the replay chipped in 142,000 more.
On social media, the awards accounted for 159 million video views across platforms, up 8 percent year to year.

articles.title_zh: Meta’s Smart Glasses PR Cleanup Campaign Is in Full Swing
articles.content_orig:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is continuing his metaverse while simultaneously pushing forward on AI agents.
At Meta Connect , the Facebook co-founder revealed on Wednesday the Meta VR Glasses, a smaller and slimmer device compared to the company's older Quest-branded family of VR headsets, and a handheld device called the Muse Charm that works with the company's recently released Muse AI personal agent . He revealed the products while speaking on stage at the annual Connect conference for developers.
Zuckerberg shared few details about what Muse Charm can do, only to say that people will be able to speak to the gadget to interact with their Meta AI agents "without having to unlock a phone or open an app." He didn't say how much it would cost, but said that Meta needs to "finalize laying out the components" and is "planning to have this ready to ship in time for the holidays in December."
"We've packed a lot of technology with this little guy," Zuckerberg said. "So, if you're not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show it what's going on around you."
The Meta VR Glasses are slimmer and lighter than the company's older Quest-branded VR headsets, but they are also more expensive, costing $1,299 when they go on sale in spring 2027. They represent Meta's first VR device since 2024, when the company debuted the $299 Quest 3S. The Meta VR Glasses are powered by an external puck that houses a Qualcomm processor and battery, allowing it to function as a mini-computer that also helps reduce the glasses' overall weight and size. The glasses are able to display better visuals than the older Quest headset, and contain sensors that track users' eyes and hand movements, which reduces the need to use controllers to interact with the device.
"We have built a new kind of VR device that delivers the same magical feeling of presence and immersion, high-resolution displays and views of the world around you in a form factor that is a pair of glasses for the first time," Zuckerberg said.

articles.title_orig: Bose launched wired, yes, wired, earbuds with ANC for $99
articles.title_zh: Bose launched wired, yes, wired, earbuds with ANC for $99
articles.content_orig:
The new Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds connect via USB-C and work with almost any device.
Bose wants to get back to basics, it seems – it just launched a new pair of wired earbuds with ANC , citing a rise in wired listening popularity. The earbuds connect to any USB-C device, using an internal, proprietary DSP to ensure they work in just about any USB-C port. With any source input, the earbuds output a fixed 24bit signal.
Bose is well-known for its Quiet Comfort lineup in recent years, but it didn’t start there. Still, the company can be considered one of the main players responsible for quality ANC in wireless headphones. After all, the QC35’s became the go-to travel option for some time.
This release, however, has literal strings attached. It needs USB-C to operate, not a 3.5mm output as most wired enthusiasts prefer at a minimum. That means you wouldn’t be able to use your own DAC/amp setup.
Even still, Bose’s Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds will be a good option for those who need ANC without the battery anxiety. Bose says the earbuds have two microphones on each bud to power active noise cancellation. Quiet Mode blocks most noise out, and Aware Mode acts as a transparency setting. ANC can also be disabled.
The new wired Bose earbuds are available to pre-order starting today for $99 in Black and White Smoke. Bose says the buds will begin shipping on October 15 for those who order from the official website and Best Buy.
